Voice typing can now write more concisely, and your dictionary follows you to the phone.

**Polish is a choice of style.** Settings → Voice typing has three options instead of an on/off switch:

- **Off** types exactly what was recognised.
- **Tidy** is what polish did before: filler, false starts and repetition go, lists are laid out, and every point you made stays. Still the default.
- **Concise** also drops verbal tics, hedges and small talk, and writes the shortest sentences that keep every fact, number, name and request. It runs on a larger model.

Your earlier setting carries over: polish on becomes Tidy, off stays Off. Voice typing history shows which style produced each entry.

**The dictionary syncs with your Parley account.** Phrases and the misheard forms they correct are shared with Parley on iPhone (1.30 and later), so a word you teach on one device is recognised on the other. Sync runs at launch, after any change (including edits made through the MCP tools), and when you return to the window. Settings → Dictionary shows when it last synced.
